description.value: Little June is a neighbourhood café nestled in the heritage building at the heart of Fernwood Square, one of Victoria's most distinctive communities. Founded by a former bush pilot who learned to roast coffee in a Yellowknife bathroom at -40°, it serves an entirely house-made menu of breakfast and lunch dishes built around seasonal ingredients from local farms. The cosy spot draws on its 110-year-old building's history while offering everything from grab-and-go baked goods to lingering egg dishes and locally sourced beer and wine.

Menu items confirm vegetarian and gluten-free options ('Roasted veggie and Havarti sandwich', 'gluten free oat' cookie). No bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or Wi-Fi are mentioned on the website; OSM notes internet_access=no but per rules this is not treated as authoritative without website confirmation. The OSM opening_hours tag reads '07:00-05:00' (implying 5 AM close), while the website clearly states 7:00 AM–5:00 PM — a likely typo in OSM (05:00 should be 17:00), flagged as a concern.
concerns: OSM opening_hours tag reads 'Mo-Su 07:00-05:00' (implying a 5:00 AM close), but the website states 'Open daily 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM'. This is almost certainly a typo in OSM where 05:00 should be 17:00.
Phone number (250) 590-7307 appears only on the website; OSM has no phone field — added from website source.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating café in a notable Victoria neighbourhood with a full menu and confirmed contact details. Clear value to touring cyclists as a breakfast/lunch stop.
enrichment_extras.notes: Outdoor seating confirmed by both OSM tag (outdoor_seating=yes) and the website gallery/context. Beer and wine available, sourced locally.
